rules.title: Relocation assistance and LAHD filing for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO
rules.requirement: Before evicting for a no-fault reason from an RSO or JCO unit, a landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD. Only then may the landlord serve the termination notice, and a copy must be filed with LAHD within 3 days. The landlord must pay relocation assistance per unit within 15 days of serving the notice, either directly or through an escrow account.
rules.key_value: Jul 1, 2026–Jun 30, 2027 amounts: Eligible $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); Qualified $23,150 / $27,400; Mom & Pop owner/family move-in $10,550 eligible / $21,250 qualified; JCO single-family dwelling owned by natural person: one month's rent. Payment due within 15 days of notice.
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).
rules.coverage_text: Units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Demolition and conversions under LAMC 47.06 and 47.07 are covered whether or not the property is subject to the RSO or JCO.
rules.exemptions: No relocation is owed when replacing a resident manager with another resident manager, unless the manager-tenant receives free or reduced rent and no other compensation. No relocation is owed for an eviction required by hazardous conditions from a natural disaster not caused by landlord negligence. A landlord may offset accumulated unpaid rent, except where the termination is required by a government order to vacate or an order for an unpermitted dwelling. Mom & Pop properties pay reduced amounts for owner or relative move-ins if all of these apply: the building has 4 or fewer units; the provision was not used in the prior 3 years; the landlord owns no more than 4 units plus a single-family home in LA; and the relative owns no LA residential property.
rules.penalty: Failing to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO. Non-payment of relocation is an affirmative defense to eviction, and the tenant may file an LAHD complaint or pursue a private right of action.
rules.extraction_note: The effective_date reflects the July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 relocation amount schedule. The amounts increase every July 1. The underlying ordinance enactment dates are not stated. LAHD administrative filing fees ($623/$1002 relocation service fees, among others) are agency fees, not tenant application screening fees, so they are not extracted as a separate category.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition of Protected Units for new construction
rules.requirement: A landlord who terminates tenancies to demolish Protected Units for new construction must file with LAHD and serve and file the notice within 3 business days. The landlord must pay relocation at the higher of the state Housing Crisis Act or City amounts: RSO/JCO amounts within 15 days, enhanced for lower-income tenants under one of three RPO relocation options.
rules.key_value: Chart B RPO standardized payments (Jul 1, 2026–Jun 30, 2027): Extremely Low Income $115,480; Very Low Income $96,750; Low Income $87,450; above low income get Chart A RSO/JCO amounts. Penalties start at $250,000 per displaced unit.
rules.citation: LA Resident Protections Ordinance, Ordinances #188481 and #188482; LAMC 165.03.I(1); LAMC 151.22-151.28; Cal. Gov. Code 66300 et seq., 66300.6(b)(4)(A)
rules.quoted_span:
Failure to comply with the RPO may result in 
financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.coverage_text: Protected Units demolished for new construction within 5 years after filing the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict. Protected Units include all RSO units, units with affordability covenants or rent control within the past 5 years, units rented by lower-income households within the past 5 years, and units withdrawn under the Ellis Act within the past 10 years.
rules.exemptions: The regular RSO/JCO relocation rules apply instead if the demolished units are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower-income tenant.
rules.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit, plus withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.interaction: Landlords must pay the higher of the state Housing Crisis Act relocation amount or the City's RPO/RSO/JCO amount. The RPO codifies and expands the HCA rather than displacing it.
rules.conflict_note: Bulletin B's Application Relocation Services Fees Chart is labeled effective July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. Bulletin A (rev. 07/01/2026) lists the same fees as effective July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Bulletin A also says the notice copy is due within 3 days, while Bulletin B says 3 business days.
rules.extraction_note: The text states the RPO was adopted by City Council on February 11, 2025 and is 'effective 2/11/2025'. The Chart B amounts are effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 and increase each July 1.
